> 道生一，一生二，二生三，三生萬物。萬物負陰而抱陽，沖氣以為和.

Two sentences, and they contain the only place in the book where the order of generation is laid out: 道, 一, 二, 三, 萬物.

Chapter 2 spread out the 二 — six pairs, each half defining the other. This chapter explains why the 二 can keep generating: between the two ends there must be a gap that has been opened, and the old name for that gap is 三.

三 is not a third thing. It is the space.

## 道生一

Not arithmetic. 一 is the undivided — the state before the pair has separated. 無極凝為太極: the limitless condenses into a pole.

Once there is a pole, there is an axis, and an axis has two ends.

## 一生二

二 is the pair. Not two objects, but a relation: high and low, before and after, sound and silence. Each half exists only in contrast with the other.

Chapter 2's whole argument was that this is how the naming works — and the naming is how we live. The 二 is not a cosmological stage; it is the structure of every distinction we make.

## 二生三

This is the link that gets flattened into a sequence of numbers, and it is the one that matters.

Two ends alone produce nothing. They sit opposed, and opposition is a standoff. What makes generation possible is the space between them — the field that the two ends hold open by not closing on each other.

三 is that opened space. It is produced by the 二, and it is not one of them.

Which is why the count is 三 and not 四: there is no fourth item. There is the one, the two, and the gap that the two enclose.

## 三生萬物

Everything else is what happens in that gap. The 三 is not a stage; it is the condition under which anything can arise.

## 負陰而抱陽

> 萬物負陰而抱陽，沖氣以為和.

Everything carries 陰 on its back and embraces 陽.

負 is to carry on the back — the passive side, what is borne. 抱 is to hold in the arms — the active side, what is held toward.

Every thing has both: what it rests on and what it reaches toward. Neither is optional.

## 沖氣以為和

沖 is to surge, to move through — the movement of the two meeting.

氣 is the medium: not air as we mean it, but the stuff that fills the gap and transmits.

和 — harmony. And this is the same 和 as chapter 29's 和/合 distinction: different things, each keeping its own nature, producing something together.

The sentence is precise: 和 is what the surging of the two produces, not what a third party imposes on them. Nothing is homogenized. The two remain two, and the space between them becomes alive.

## Why the gap must stay empty

If the space between the two ends is filled, the generation stops. Chapter 11 already said it in objects: fill the hub's bore and you have a sculpture of a wheel.

So the practical reading of 二生三 is the same as the practical reading of chapter 11 — keep the space. A pair that has been resolved into one side has no gap; it has a conclusion. And a conclusion does not generate.
